Subject: Pricing question for Dedicated onboarding

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the product demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency profiles and the cost controls. We're starting to evaluate a move from your hosted API into a Dedicated pool for production workloads (sensitive PHI routing will require a VPC later). Before we tee up procurement, two asks: 

1) We run a fairly spiky inference workload. Can you outline your recommended GPU pool sizing for an initial production deployment?  We currently average ~20M tokens/day (peak ~40M) across 3 services; most requests are 512 tokens or less.

2) Commercially: our CFO wants to understand how Redwood treats hosted spend when customers migrate to Dedicated. Are there conversion credits, bridge months, or invoice offsets that we can expect to smooth the transition while we commit to reserved capacity? If you have a standard formula or examples, that would be super helpful.

Procurement attached the RFP for context (procurement_RFP.pdf). We aim to finalize commercial terms by end of month — can we get a short note on options + a rough commercial sketch?

Best,
Nadia
Nadia Flores
Director, Platform Engineering
Stellar Health
From: laura.bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Nadia Flores <nadia@stellarhealth.com>
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing question for Dedicated onboarding

Hi Nadia — thanks for the note and the RFP. Quick summary below and a couple of options we typically use for migrations like this. I'll attach a short pricing worksheet for your procurement team (draft_pricing_sheet.xlsx).

High level sizing recommendation (initial):
- Start with a two-node A100-80GB pool (N=2) for predictable throughput; recommend reserving burst slots for short-lived spikes.
- Target throughput guarantee: 160-200 tokens/sec sustained per GPU for ~512-context gen workloads; this covers most of your peak profile while keeping cost predictable.
- If you expect sustained + large multimodal runs, we can size one additional node as a hot-standby.

Commercial migration options (pick one):
A) Conversion-credit model (preferred for steady hosted spend): take the trailing-3-month hosted spend, apply a 65% conversion credit (applied as monthly offsets against Dedicated invoice) spread across the first 6 months of the commit.
B) Bridge-months model (preferred for big short-term spikes): Redwood offers up to 2 bridge months of free or discounted capacity (50–75% credit) to cover the transition period while Dedicated pools warm up.
C) Invoice offset (finance): one-time onboarding credit (negotiable) applied to the first invoice; useful for short-term procurement constraints.

Trade-offs: A gives smoother monthly economics and aligns incentives; B is simpler but front-loaded; C is the most flexible but requires approval from finance.

I'll loop Marcus and Rishi on the pricing details and ask finance to pre-clear a moderate onboarding credit so we can move fast. If you like, we can put together a formal commercial sketch (commit size, term, credit phasing) for procurement tomorrow.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

Team — forwarding Nadia's RFP and procurement ask. Below my proposed commercial sketch; wanted your quick read on risk and margin before I send the formal proposal.

Proposed sketch (economic):
- Target commit: $120k/month for 12 months (predictable reserved capacity).
- Onboarding credit: up to $60k one-time (invoice offset) OR conversion-credit equal to 65% of trailing 3 months hosted spend, capped at $60k, applied over first 6 months.
- Bridge months: 2 months @ 70% credit for reserved capacity (if Stellar prefers block credits rather than spread conversion credits).
- Throughput SLA: minimum sustained throughput of 160 tokens/sec per GPU for 512 context (financially backed: credits for >2 consecutive minutes below SLA).
- GPU pool: start N=2 A100-80GB; option to scale to N=3 after 30 days with automatic pro rata billing.

Notes/questions for internal ops/finance:
- Marcus: does $60k cap make sense from a financial risk perspective? Might need to shrink to $45k if we want to preserve margin on a 12-mo commit.
- Rishi: sales ask — would a 9-month term be common? They may push shorter; we should have a 9-mo with slightly higher price per month fallback.

If we're aligned I can craft proposal and include both options (12-mo with $60k onboarding / 9-mo with $40k onboarding + slightly higher unit price).

—Laura

Hi Nadia — attached is a short commercial proposal that lays out two options so procurement can pick the path that best fits internal approval (proposal_Stellar_Health_v1.pdf). Key points in plain language: 

Option A — 12-month reserved commit (recommended)
- Monthly commit: $120,000/month for 12 months
- Onboarding: $60,000 credit applied as $20,000/mo across months 1–3 (invoice offsets)
- Bridge months: we include 2 bridge months where up to 70% of dedicated capacity is credited if needed
- Throughput guarantee: 160 tokens/sec sustained per GPU; credits issued for sustained breaches (details in SLA appendix)
- Pool: start N=2 A100-80GB, ability to scale to N=3 after 30d (pro rata)

Option B — 9-month soft-commit (shorter term)
- Monthly commit: $140,000/month for 9 months (higher rate to mitigate shorter term)
- Onboarding: $40,000 credit applied as invoice offset across months 1–2
- Bridge months: 1 bridge month @ 60% credit

Other commercial mechanics:
- Conversion-credit formula (if they prefer): trailing-3-mo hosted spend * 0.65, applied as monthly offsets across the first 6 months; capped at onboarding credit above.
- Finance can issue a one-time invoice credit if procurement requires a single-line credit rather than monthly offsets.

Next steps:
1) If this looks acceptable, I'll send the DocuSign link (we can pre-fill SOW and attachment references).
2) If procurement needs different phasing, we can present both options side-by-side in a short one-pager for the CFO.
